BILL AUTHOR SUBJECT
AB 109 Gabriel Budget Act of 2026
SENATE COMMITTEE ON BUDGET AND FISCAL REVIEW
Senator John Laird, Chair
2025 - 2026 Regular
Bill No: AB 109 Hearing Date: June 15, 2026
Author: Gabriel
Version: June 11, 2026 Amended
Urgency: No Fiscal: Yes
Consultant: Elisa Wynne
Subject: Budget Act of 2026
Summary: This bill contains the Budget Act of 2026. This bill represents a budget
package that authorizes General Fund expenditures of $253 billion and assumes
$285.5 billion in total General Fund resources. Under this budget act, there are
combined total reserves of $36.5 billion, with $15.1 billion in the Budget Stabilization
Account (BSA), $4.5 billion in the Special Fund for Economic Uncertainties (SFEU),
$9.5 billion in the Proposition 98 Rainy Day Fund, and $7.4 billion in the Surplus Set-
aside for 2027-28.
Background: This reflects a legislative agreement on a budget plan that reflects a
balanced budget for both the 2026-27 and 2027-28 fiscal years, despite the difficult
choices the state faces in this budget and future years. Specifically, this bill reflects the
2026-27 budget as detailed below.
Proposed Law:
K-12 Education
1) Augments funding for special education programs by $2.4 billion, which is a 43
percent increase above levels appropriated in the 2025 Budget Act.
2) Provides an increase of $60 million Proposition 98 General Fund for the special
education extraordinary costs pool.
3) Provides an increase of $20 million for special education and related services to
pupils with low-incidence disabilities.
4) Provides a 2.87 percent cost-of-living adjustment for various TK-12 categorical
programs.
5) Appropriates $552,000 General Fund ongoing for the Department of Education to
support the implementation of the single reimbursement rate structure for the
California State Preschool Program.
6) Appropriates $910,000 General Fund annually for the next three years for the
Office of State Audits and Evaluations in the Department of Finance to help
support the California State Preschool Program audits.
AB 109 (Gabriel) Page 2 of 25
7) Appropriates $178,000 General Fund and one position to support the
Department of Education’s oversight responsibilities of county offices of
education.
8) Appropriates $850,000 General Fund ongoing for state salaries of employees
working on the federal Title I, Part A program.
9) Appropriates $1.2 million federal Individuals with Disabilities Education Act
(IDEA) funds and three positions to support increased state monitoring of out-of-
state nonpublic schools.
10) Appropriates $16.2 million federal IDEA funds on an ongoing basis to support
special education teachers, and $1.6 million federal IDEA funds to support
grants, through the Golden State Teachers Grant Program, administered by the
California Student Aid Commission.
11) Appropriates $4.7 billion Proposition 98 General Fund for the Expanded Learning
Opportunities Program, guaranteeing a base rate of at least $1,800 for Tier 2
local educational agencies.
12) Appropriates $4 million General Fund one-time for deferred maintenance projects
at the State Special Schools.
13) Makes various technical adjustments to conform with federal grants, available
special funds, and program administration.
14) Appropriates $20 million in federal carryover funds for adult education health
pathways.
15) Adds reporting language for funds administered for online educational materials.
16) Consolidates the administration of the California State Preschool Program and
shifts $1 billion of non-local educational agency administered State Preschool
Programs for a total program cost of $2.7 billion Proposition 98 General Fund for
California State Preschool.
17) Appropriates $20 million Proposition 98 General Fund for the Quality Rating
Improvement System Grants.
18) Appropriates $5 million in federal funds for Save the Children.
19) Appropriates $2.8 billion in federal funds and $1.9 billion Proposition 98 General
Fund to support universal school meals.
20) Funds mandated costs for local educational agencies serving grades 6 through
12 to stock all women’s restrooms with menstrual products through the K-12
Mandate Block Grant.
AB 109 (Gabriel) Page 3 of 25
21) Re-appropriates $1 billion Proposition 98 General Fund for various programs,
including the discretionary block grant, grants to support students experiencing
homelessness, and others.
Higher Education
22) Rejects $1.1 million ongoing General Fund related to increased building rental
expenses at the California State Library.
23) Includes the reappropriation of $94.3 million General Fund from the Local Library
Infrastructure Grant program, at the California State Library, for the same
purposes and extends the encumbrance and expenditure period to June 30,
2030.
24) Includes $254.3 million ongoing General Fund to support a five percent base
increase, representing the fifth and final year of the Compact at the University of
California (UC).
25) Includes $96.3 million ongoing General Fund, to support a two percent base
increase, representing a partial payment of the fourth year of the Compact at the
UC.
26) Includes provisional language clarifying the annual target of replacing 902
nonresident undergraduate students with resident undergraduate students is a
total target of 4,510 students across the five years of the Compact. Additionally
includes provisional language authorizing the Director of the Department of
Finance to proportionally reduce funding if the UC falls short of the enrollment
swap target.
27) Includes $61 million ongoing General Fund to support replacement of 902
nonresident undergraduate students with resident undergraduate students at
three high-demand campuses. This is inclusive of the one-time deferral of this
funding from 2025-26 and the increase as part of the fifth-year Compact payment
at the UC.
28) Includes restoration of $130 million ongoing General Fund, related to a one-time
deferral from 2025-26. Additionally delays the repayment of the one-time deferral
from 2026-27 to 2027-28 and renews the option for a zero-interest loan in 2026-
27 at the UC.

target of 2,968 Full-Time Equivalent Students (FTES), for a total target of
212,503 FTES at the UC.

Youth Cohorts at UC campuses.

46) Includes an additional $132.1 million Proposition 98 General Fund to support

Resources
61) Sets aside $2.6 billion Safe Drinking Water, Wildfire Prevention, Drought
Preparedness, and Clean Air Bond Act of 2024 (Proposition 4) funding in 2026-
27 with details to be worked out in a future budget bill.
62) Maintains 356.2 vacant Full-Time Equivalents (FTEs) ($39.8 million Special
Fund) at various departments, including 60.1 FTEs at the Department of Fish and
Wildlife (CDFW), 15 FTEs ($2.9 million Special Fund) at the Department of
Pesticide Regulation, 29 FTEs ($5.7 million Special Fund) at the State Water
Resources Control Board (SWRCB), 75.1 FTEs ($10.6 million Special Fund) at
the Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC), nine FTEs ($1.2 million
Special Fund) at the Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery
(CalRecycle), and seven FTEs ($1.3 million Special Fund) at the California Public
Utilities Commission (CPUC).
63) Appropriates $719,000 Timber Regulation and Forest Restoration Fund (TRFRF)
and $1.8 million in reimbursement authority in 2026-27 and ongoing resources in
future years to the Department of Conservation (DOC), CDFW, California
Coastal Commission, and SWRCB to support the expedited review and
implementation of vegetation management to reduce fire risk statewide. The bill
appropriates $250,000 TRFRF in 2026-27 and ongoing to the California Natural
Resources Agency (CNRA) for information technology support to address
application intake and vegetation treatment tracking needs. This bill requires
CNRA (and relevant departments) to report back to the Legislature on outcomes
of and lessons learned from the State of Emergency-expedited vegetation
management process.
64) Appropriates $6.24 million General Fund and adds 31 positions starting in 2026-
27, and ongoing resources in future years to the California Department of
Forestry and Fire Protection (CalFire) to support the state inspection goal of
250,000 annual parcel inspections. Of these amounts annually, $958,000
represents the statutory proportional share for the six Contract Counties.
65) Appropriates $11.66 million General Fund in 2026-27 ($10.79 million General
Fund ongoing) to the California Conservation Corps (CCC) and adds 49 positions
and 47 full-time equivalent Corpsmember and Special Corpsmember positions to
implement a year-round, seven-day per week schedule that provides relief and
support positions to allow CCC to align with CalFire’s Hand Crew Program
schedule.
66) Appropriates up to $66.5 million General Fund annually in 2026-27 through 2028-
29, $69.64 million in 2029-30, and $74.15 million ongoing to CalFire for fixed-
wing pilot and mechanics contract-cost increases.
